_README: VERIFIED CARRIER QUOTES. One entry per quote actually obtained from Pirate Ship — never an
estimate, never an interpolation, never a number carried over from a different lane.
This file does NOT drive the site yet. script.js and db/orders.py still use the flat
SHIPPING_TIERS ladder. Switching the code to read zone-aware rates is blocked on two things
only the owner can settle: the origin ZIP (without it a destination cannot be mapped to a
zone at all) and the cart-versus-charge decision in STRIPE.md. Until then this file is the
place verified quotes accumulate so none is lost or quietly generalised.
Ground Advantage is priced on TWO axes: billable weight (rounded up to the pound above 1 lb)
and zone (distance from origin to destination). One quote fills exactly one cell. A quote for
8 oz to one ZIP says nothing about 3 lb, and nothing about a different zone.
Fields on each quote:
price_usd     what Pirate Ship quoted, exactly as shown
oz            the weight entered to get that quote
band          which ladder band that weight falls in ('sub' = under 1 lb, else the pound)
dest_zip      the destination entered
zone          the USPS zone that origin->dest resolves to; null until origin_zip is known
weighed       true only if the parcel was on a scale. false means the weight was estimated,
which makes the quote provisional: the real parcel may bill in another band.
dims_in       box dimensions used, if any. Ground Advantage applies dimensional weight to
large-but-light parcels, so a quote taken without dims can be low.
collected     when it was taken. Carrier rates change; a stale quote is not a verified one.
source        where it came from.

_zone_policy_options.flat: One price per weight band for every destination. What the site does today. Simplest, and wrong at both ends of the country.
_zone_policy_options.banded: Group zones — e.g. near (1-4), mid (5-6), far (7-9). Three quotes per weight instead of nine.
_zone_policy_options.full: A price per weight band per zone 1-9. Most accurate, most quotes to collect.

quotes.source: Pirate Ship calculator, sample quote supplied by owner
notes: REFERENCE ONLY, by the owner's instruction. Not applied to any band.
Two things keep it out of the table: the zone is inferred and unconfirmed, and the 8 oz was
Pirate Ship shows the zone on the quote screen — confirm it there and set zone_verified.
For comparison the site charges $5.50 flat under 1 lb, so this lane looks ~$0.32 low.
quotes.zone_inference_basis: 85641 -> 90210 is about 450 miles, and USPS zone 4 covers 301-600 miles. Distance is how zones are broadly set, but the published chart is by ZIP prefix pair and is authoritative.

origin_note: Vail, AZ. The ONLY place an origin belongs: shipping_cents() in db/orders.py and shippingFor() in script.js take weight and nothing else, so writing 85641 into either would be decoration, not configuration. When the zone engine is built it reads the origin from here.

near.note: roughly AZ, NM, SoCal, NV, UT, west TX from 85641

mid.note: roughly the mountain west, plains, central states

far.note: roughly the east coast, upper midwest, and AK/HI/territories

_zone_group_warning: Those geographies are a STARTING POINT for choosing a destination to quote, not a zone chart. Pirate Ship prints the actual zone on every quote — read it there and record it, rather than trusting the description.

rate_table._note: null means no quote yet. Nothing here is inferred from a neighbouring cell, and no cell is filled by interpolation. 1 lb is absent on purpose: no basket of 7/10/32/40 oz goods plus 3 oz packaging weighs exactly 16 oz, so that band is unreachable.

_zone_map_README: USPS zone for a destination, keyed by the first THREE digits of its ZIP. Empty, and it must
be filled from the published chart — a zone is not computable from distance, and I will not
guess one. Get it from postcalc.usps.com/DomesticZoneChart with origin 856: it returns every
destination prefix and its zone, which is exactly this mapping.
Example of the shape once filled: {"902": 4, "100": 8, "606": 6}
UNTIL THIS IS POPULATED, ZONE PRICING IS OFF and the flat ladder runs — see
zone_pricing_ready() in db/orders.py. A half-filled map would quote some buyers by zone and
others by the flat table, which is worse than either.
